findings.summary: The HTTP group regex requires a literal ':' right after each prefix, so it matches only groups with no sub-namespace. Helidon -- the one library architecture.md rule 5 names by name -- publishes under io.helidon.webserver / io.helidon.common / io.helidon.http, none of which match. The gate cannot catch the dependency it was written to catch.
findings.failure_scenario: Executed: grep -oE "($HTTP_GROUPS):[a-z0-9.-]+" over a dependency report containing io.helidon.webserver:helidon-webserver:4.2.0, io.helidon.common:helidon-common:4.2.0, io.helidon.http:helidon-http:4.2.0, org.eclipse.jetty.ee10:jetty-ee10-servlet:12.0.16, org.apache.httpcomponents.client5:httpclient5:5.4 and jakarta.servlet.jsp:jakarta.servlet.jsp-api:3.1.1 returns exactly one hit: io.netty:netty-common. When M1 adds `implementation(libs.helidon.webserver)` to `ingest`, ingest resolves Helidon, the gate prints 'stay inside their dependency surface' and exits 0. The author's own verification used io.netty and software.amazon.awssdk -- the two groups in the list that happen to have no sub-namespace -- so the hole was invisible to it. Anchor on the group boundary instead, e.g. (^|[^a-zA-Z0-9._-])(io\.helidon|...)([.][a-z0-9.]+)?:.

findings.summary: The exit status of the `dependencies` invocation is discarded and stderr is sent to /dev/null. Any failure leaves $deps empty, both greps find nothing, and the gate reports success for a module whose classpath it never read.
findings.failure_scenario: Executed against the real build: `deps=$(./gradlew :format:dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath --console=plain -q 2>/dev/null)` with a configuration name the module does not have exits 1 with DEPS_LEN=0; the subsequent `[ -n "$hits" ]` is false and the module passes. Real triggers: a module that is not yet a java-library (no runtimeClasspath configuration), a Gradle daemon killed by WSL2 under the 512m caps build.md warns about, a corrupt cache, or a repository timeout resolving the dependency. All three yield the green line '8 module(s) build, test, and stay inside their dependency surface' -- a claim about bytes never examined (non-negotiable 4). Check the status, and assert the report is non-empty and contains the 'runtimeClasspath -' header before trusting an empty hit set.

findings.summary: Delta routing derives module names from the first path segment, so the three places that change every module's resolved classpath without touching any module directory -- buildSrc/, gradle/libs.versions.toml, and the root build.gradle.kts -- select zero modules and the gate exits 0 on 'no module changed'.
findings.failure_scenario: Executed: piping buildSrc/src/main/kotlin/binjava.java-conventions.gradle.kts and gradle/libs.versions.toml through the sed produces only 'gradle' (buildSrc matches nothing at all, since [a-z-]* cannot span the capital S), and neither survives the ALL filter, so MODULES is empty. The convention plugin already injects a `dependencies { ... }` block into every module; a commit that adds a Helidon or okhttp entry there, or bumps a catalog coordinate whose transitive graph now pulls netty, touches no module directory and the gate passes vacuously. Map buildSrc/, gradle/, settings.gradle.kts and build.gradle.kts to the full ALL set.

findings.summary: The HTTP rule is applied to every module except `http`, but architecture.md rule 5 enumerates four (format, binstore-spi, sequencer, ingest). The extra module caught by the widening is `binstore-backends`, whose stated contents are S3, GCS and Azure -- every one of which drags an HTTP client onto runtimeClasspath.
findings.failure_scenario: software.amazon.awssdk:s3 pulls software.amazon.awssdk:netty-nio-client, which pulls io.netty:netty-*; the apache-client variant pulls org.apache.httpcomponents; the GCS and Azure SDKs pull netty via grpc/reactor. The moment M1 lands the S3 backend, `binstore-backends` fails rule 5 with 'Two front doors, one implementation. If this module needs HTTP, the decision it is making belongs in `ingest`' -- advice that is wrong for a module whose entire job is talking to the object store. The next author's cheapest exits are to widen the `!= http` exemption or drop a group from HTTP_GROUPS, both of which weaken the gate for everyone (non-negotiable 2). Scope the HTTP rule to the four modules the standard names, or exempt backends explicitly with the reason written down.

findings.summary: The usage block says a no-argument invocation checks 'every module'. With the default GATE_SCOPE=delta it checks only changed modules and frequently checks none.
findings.failure_scenario: A developer or agent runs `scripts/check-module.sh` with a dirty tree touching only docs, reads 'every module' in the header, and records that all eight modules were verified when the script printed 'no module changed'. lib.sh built scope_note precisely so a delta pass never reads like a full one; the header undoes it. Say 'every changed module; GATE_SCOPE=full for all eight'.
